sourceRoles.title: Price sources
sourceRoles.info: Where values come from, per kind of item: a reference source is valued first and is the source items should be linked to; supporting sources are used when the reference has too few sales; comparison sources are shown beside the value, never in it. The roles come from the sources' plug-ins (suggested) and apply to every account.
sourceRoles.adminOnly: Only an admin can change them.

quality.unverified: Unverified: {count} items in common with {reference} (10 needed)

sourceRoles.suggestedWhy: The role the source's plug-in suggests: its author's tested setup, not a measurement. The evidence is the check under each supporting source: how its sales compare with the reference's on the same items.
sourceRoles.perClass: Each kind of item has its own roles and order. Within a role, the arrows set the order: values try sources sharing a role in this order (with two references, the first one is the main one), and item pages list them in it. Values and the value history follow a change within seconds.
sourceRoles.asksOnly: Asking or store prices, not sales: usually above what items sell for.

markets.title: Markets
markets.info: The value counts the primary market's sources only. The secondary market gives one price per item to compare with (the reference source's, else a supporting one's). Applies to every account.
markets.secondaryInfo: Shown beside the value, never in it.
markets.compareInfo: Other markets' prices are converted to the base currency and never count in the value.

identity.what: An identity page is one stable product page that says exactly what an item is: its name, set, number and picture (e.g. a card's page on a card marketplace).
identity.why: It is the item's ID card. Once an item is linked to it, Tora knows precisely which item it is and can find the same item on every other source, so prices are matched to the right item. Without one, matches are guesses from the name.
identity.how: Pick one source per kind of item and market. Items without an identity page are listed under Actions. A product page from another source of the same market that has them counts too. It does not have to be the price reference.
identity.primaryNotice: Items without an identity page in {market} show under Actions as "without an identity link".
identity.secondaryNotice: Items without an identity page in {market} show under Actions with their own notice type (blue by default).
identity.notListed: Only sources with one product page per item can be identity pages. Search-based sources (flea markets, auctions, eBay) cannot, but they can still be any market's price reference: set that under Price sources.
identity.otherNotice: Items without an identity page in {market} are not flagged.
identity.amountInfo: Cards and sealed TCG always need an identity link. Other items only when they cost more than this ({amount} now).

currency.title: Currencies
currency.info: Every amount is stored in the base currency. Prices in other currencies are converted with the exchange rate of their day when they are collected.
currency.baseInfo: Every amount is stored in it. Choose it when setting up, before adding anything: any currency, usually your primary market's. Changing it later converts every stored amount, and is offered only for a currency with exchange rates (another market's).
currency.noOthers: Every source prices in the base currency: no exchange rates needed.
currency.missing: No rate yet: prices in this currency are not saved until one is set. Pick a rate source (rates arrive with the next collect) or type a rate.
currency.manualInfo: Used from today until changed; earlier days keep their rates.
currency.confirm: Convert every stored amount ({count}) from {from} to {to}, each with the exchange rate of its own date? Values are rebuilt right after. Do it while no collect is running.
currency.noPlugins: No rate plug-in covers {code} yet. Plug-ins are listed after the home PC's next collect; until then you can type a rate.

languages.title: Languages
languages.info: The app is shown in the primary language to anyone who has not chosen; everyone switches between the two with the language toggle. Picked from the installed translation files.
languages.add: {count, plural, one {# language installed} other {# languages installed}}. Another one is a translation of messages/en.json added to the app (the setup guide explains how).
languages.primaryInfo: Shown first, and to people signing in.
languages.secondaryInfo: The other side of the toggle.

boardTracking.title: Board tracker hours
boardTracking.info: Store feeds (a userscript in a browser) read their boards only within these hours, like a person would, not around the clock. Outside them the feed stops: it reloads no page and reads no posts, replies or pictures, and asks Tora every minute or so whether to start again. For every account.
boardTracking.always: Off: feeds read their boards around the clock.
boardTracking.delayInfo: Drawn again each day, so the tracker never starts or stops on the minute (up to an hour).
boardTracking.warning: Tora may start late and finish early: it starts reading {min} to {max} seconds after {from} and stops {min} to {max} seconds before {to}, at another time each day.
boardTracking.outside: Outside the hours, the Stores pages say so in red, and admins can track for an hour or until the next start (once: the hours go on as usual after).
boardTracking.invalid: Two different times, and delays from 0 to 3600 seconds, the shortest first.

timeZone.title: Time zone
timeZone.info: The app's time zone: it decides when a day starts for the daily value snapshots, charts, value windows and the collect's once a day, and every time is shown in it. One zone for every account, usually the admin's own. Pick it at setup, next to the base currency.
timeZone.confirm: Change the time zone from {from} to {to}? Every stored time is rewritten as the same moment in the new zone, then values and the daily history are rebuilt (a minute or two). Do it while no collect is running.
timeZone.changeInfo: Changing it later is rare (e.g. after moving abroad): stored times keep their moment, and days near midnight may move to the day before or after.
timeZone.setupInfo: No lots, prices or history yet: changing it now only rewrites the app's own records (accounts, sets, settings).

categories.title: Categories
categories.info: What kinds of items the app holds. Each category has kinds (e.g. booster box, single) and fields; each kind has a condition list, which decides how lots are described and which prices value them. Names are typed in the app's languages.
categories.plugins: Collectors say which categories they collect; a new category needs a collector that prices it (the setup guide explains how). Price sources and identity pages are set per category and condition list.
categories.items: {count, plural, =0 {no items} one {# item} other {# items}}
categories.lots: {count, plural, =0 {no lots} one {# lot} other {# lots}}
categories.newKey: Key: made from the name on save
categories.name: Name
categories.hidden: Hidden: not offered for new items
categories.inUse: Used by items: hide it instead
categories.cannotRemove: Has items: it can be hidden, not removed.
categories.listsInfo: Ready-made lists (their prices come from the collectors as they are):
categories.valuesInfo: Values, best first. Values with the same pool group are valued together when one has too few sales.

touched.kind_list: {name}: {count, plural, one {# item moves} other {# items move}} to another condition list (their lots need the new condition)
touched.field_removed: Field {name}: removed from {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}
touched.choice_removed: {name}: cleared on {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}
touched.value_removed: {name}: cleared on {count, plural, one {# lot} other {# lots}}
touched.region_removed: {name}: cleared on {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}

blocked.category_in_use: A category with items cannot be removed; hide it.
blocked.kind_in_use: A kind with items cannot be removed; hide it.
blocked.list_key: A condition list needs a name.
blocked.list_empty: A condition list needs at least one value.
blocked.value_key: Two values have the same name.
blocked.no_kinds: Each category needs at least one kind.
blocked.kind_key: Two kinds have the same name.
blocked.kind_list: A kind uses a removed condition list.
blocked.field_key: Two fields have the same name.
blocked.choice_empty: A choice field needs at least one choice.
blocked.region_key: Two regions have the same name.

categories.regionsInfo: What the region field offers for this category (print language, game region, pressing country...), in order: the first is the default when an import cannot tell. Plug-ins read these keys.

database.title: Database
database.info: Rows the hosted database (Turso) read and wrote this month, as its replies report them. The free plan allows 500 million rows read and 10 million written a month.
database.read: {month}: {read} rows read of {free} free (at this pace, {projected} by the end of the month)
database.budgetInfo: The app's daily check sends an alert when the month passes this, or heads past it at this pace (from the 5th).
database.none: Nothing counted this month yet. Only the hosted database is counted: while Tora runs on a local file there is nothing to count.
database.note: Counted from Tora's own queries. Turso's dashboard has the exact total, including anything run outside Tora.

server.title: Server status
server.info: What the server runs and how it is doing, read-only. Values of secret settings and lines about sources kept from AI models are left out.
server.host: {platform}, Node {node}. Up {up} h; the app {app} h.
server.noLogs: No logs in the state folder.
server.tokenInfo: Lets a helper (Claude Code, a monitoring tool) read this status at /api/server/status without an account. It can change nothing. Keep it like a password.
server.noToken: No token: nobody can read the status from outside.
server.tokenSince: A token made {date} is in use.
server.tokenOnce: Copy it now: it is not shown again.
server.replaceConfirm: The current token stops working. Make a new one?
server.removeConfirm: Remove the token? Nobody can read the status from outside anymore.

commands.info: Commands to run on the home PC, in a terminal in the Tora folder (WSL or Linux). Nothing runs from this page: copy a command, then fill in the parts in '<'angle brackets'>'.

collect.title: Collecting prices
collect.all: Every collector: look for listings of new items, then fetch prices (listings already collected today are left out), then pictures, values and the day's snapshot.
collect.source: Only one collector (its key, e.g. ebay).
collect.product: Only one item (its ID from the item page's address).
collect.matchOnly: Only look for listings of items without one.
collect.collectOnly: Only fetch prices for listings already confirmed.
collect.refresh: Also collects listings already collected today (normally left out).
collect.valuate: Only rebuild values and the value history.

schedule.title: Daily schedule
schedule.install: Installs the Windows task: after logging on and at 12:00, retried hourly until a run finishes that day.
schedule.perMarket: One task per market at its own hour, when one night is not enough for every collector.
schedule.force: Runs the scheduled collect now, even if today's already finished.
schedule.lastLog: The end of the collect log: why the last run stopped, what each source did

imports.title: Imports and review
imports.uploads: Reads files uploaded in the app (Imports > Upload) with the home PC's Claude login.
imports.ai: Imports purchases from screenshots, PDFs or text in a folder, through Claude.
imports.mail: Imports purchases from order emails exported with Google Takeout.
imports.review: Asks Claude about flagged sales and searches; findings go to Imports > Suggestions.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.create: Creates an account: password, authenticator QR code, backup codes. The first one is an admin.
accounts.devices: Lists an account's signed-in devices (at most 2).
accounts.revoke: Signs a device out, or all of them.
accounts.twoFactor: A lost phone: new authenticator key and backup codes.
accounts.disable: Stops an account from signing in.
accounts.enable: Lets a disabled account sign in again.
accounts.demo: Fills the demo account with sample lots (only accounts named demo*).

backups.title: Backups
backups.backup: Saves today's copy of the whole database (the schedule does it after each collect), and deletes copies no longer kept: the last 30 days and the first of each month for a year are.
backups.list: Lists the copies (or the folder in BACKUP_DIR).
backups.restore: Loads a copy into the new, empty database in DATABASE_URL; it refuses a database with data.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.afterRun: Records a collect or backup that stopped before it could, and sends failures to admins at once. The schedule runs it after each collect and backup.
alerts.check: The app's morning check, run from the PC: "nothing ran" alerts and the daily summaries (each person at most once in 20 hours).

database.title: Database and Claude
database.migrate: Applies new database migrations. Run it right after pushing a change that adds one.
database.catalogFetch: Refreshes the TCG set catalog files (then review and commit them).
database.catalogSync: Loads the plug-ins' set lists now (only the regions your set categories use); the collect does it by itself when they change.
database.mcp: Lets Claude Code read your data, read-only (sources marked no-AI are left out).

myData.lotsInfo: Every lot, one per row: item, condition, quantity, cost, date, shop, order ID, status, value now and profit; sold lots with their sale. Opens in Excel, Numbers or Google Sheets.
myData.lotsImport: The same layout can be imported: <link>Imports > Spreadsheet</link>.
myData.allInfo: One JSON file with your items, lots, their history, manual prices, watchlist, linked listings and imports: for keeping a copy, or for another program.
myData.loadInfo: This account is empty: a file downloaded here (from another install, or from this one) brings back its items, lots, history, manual prices, watchlist and imports. Items this install does not have are added; their prices come with the next collect.
myData.loaded: Loaded: {lots} lots, {history} history entries, {watches} watched items and {items} items ({itemsAdded} new to this install).

loadError.format: This is not a file downloaded from Tora (All your data).
loadError.version: This file comes from another version of Tora and cannot be loaded.
loadError.currency: The file’s amounts are in another base currency than this install’s.
loadError.notEmpty: This account already has data: a file loads into an empty account only.
loadError.failed: The file could not be sent. Try again.

myData.noPrices: Prices collected from other sites are not included (their terms do not allow passing them on); each lot carries its value now instead.
myData.adminBackups: The whole database is backed up every day on the home PC (Admin preferences > Commands).

alertText.test: Tora: test message. Alerts will arrive here.
alertText.connected: Tora: alerts will arrive in this chat.
alertText.collectFailed: Tora: the nightly collect finished, but some sources had problems:
alertText.status_locked: skipped, another collect was running it
alertText.noCollect: Tora: no collect has run for {hours} hours (last: {last}). Is the home PC on?
alertText.noBackup: Tora: no backup for {hours} hours (last: {last}). Is the home PC on?
alertText.dbBudget: Tora: the database read {read} million rows this month; at this pace {projected} million by the end of the month (budget {budget} million, free plan 500 million). See Settings > Admin > Database.
alertText.sourceQuiet: Tora: {sources} found no new sales on its last 3 days of runs, though it usually finds some. Its site may have changed: look at the collect log, or open one of its listings (Settings > Collectors).
alertText.selfCheck: Tora: the nightly self-check found saved prices that did not match the collected sales, and rebuilt them: {items}. If this repeats, tell the developer.
alertText.summaryImport: {method}: {imported} added, {existing} already in Tora, {skipped} left out, {problem} with a problem

alertText.buyTarget: {name}: an ask at {price} on {source}, under your target {target}.
alertText.summaryDrops: Sharp drops (15% or more in a week):
alertText.storePosts: Tora: cards on sale in your area
alertText.feedSilent: Tora: the store feed ({source}) has been silent since {since} ({minutes} min): no store notices until it sends again. Check the feed (for a userscript: its browser tab).

alertText.feedSilentTracking: Tora: the store feed has sent nothing since tracking started at {started} ({minutes} min; its last push: {last}). No store notices until it sends. Check the feed (for a userscript: its browser tab).

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.info: Tora sends a message when something needs you: to admins at once when the collect or the backup fails or does not run, and to everyone a morning summary of imports that did not add every row and of what waits on Actions.
alerts.none: No channel yet. Add Telegram or Discord below.
alerts.testFailed: Not sent. See the error above.
alerts.telegramSteps: 1. Open the link below on a device with Telegram and press Start. 2. Come back and press Check.
alerts.telegramNoBot: Telegram is not set up yet: an admin adds the app's bot below.
alerts.discordHelp: In Discord: a channel's settings > Integrations > Webhooks > New webhook > Copy webhook URL.
alerts.mention: Your Discord user ID (to mention you)
alerts.mentionHelp: Each message mentions you, so it always notifies. Your ID: in Discord, Settings > Advanced > Developer Mode, then right-click your name > Copy User ID.
alerts.forum: A forum channel: a post per location each day, other alerts in one Tora post.
alerts.forumNoMention: In a forum channel only a message that mentions you notifies: add your Discord user ID (Settings > Advanced > Developer Mode, then right-click your name > Copy User ID).
alerts.failures: The collect or the backup failed or did not run (at once)
alerts.imports: Imports that did not add every row (morning summary)
alerts.botInfo: One bot for the whole app. In Telegram, talk to @BotFather, send /newbot, choose a name, and paste the token it gives here. Stored encrypted.
alerts.botRemoveConfirm: Remove the bot? Everyone's Telegram channels stop.
alerts.schedule: The morning check runs once a day from {time} (app time), on the server itself.
alerts.scheduleHosted: The morning check runs once a day at about {time} (Vercel cron, set in apps/web/vercel.json).

error.invalid: That does not look right. Check it and try again.
error.unreachable: Could not reach the service. Try again in a moment.
error.not_found: Tora did not find your Start message yet. Press Start in Telegram, then Check again.
error.no_bot: No Telegram bot is set up yet.
error.no_secret: AUTH_SECRET is not set on the server.

alerts.buy: Watched items: Good price, or an ask under your target (at once, after the nightly collect)
alerts.drops: Sharp drops of owned and watched items, 15% or more in a week (morning summary)
alerts.styleInfo: See every kind of message with examples, and change how it looks and reads.

alertStyle.title: Message style
alertStyle.info: Every kind of message Tora sends, with example data, as Discord and Telegram show it. Change its look and wording; the previews follow. Saved per kind, for your messages only.

kindInfo.store: Posts and comments about cards on sale at a store in your area (Stores).
kindInfo.storeUnknown: Recent posts naming no store or place Tora knows (add the code on the Stores page).
kindInfo.feed: Your store feed: connected, silent, a board back, posts maybe missed.
kindInfo.buy: A watched item at a good price, or an ask under your target (right after the nightly collect).
kindInfo.summary: The morning summary: imports that did not add every row, what waits on Actions, sharp drops.
kindInfo.admin: Admins: a failed collect or backup, nothing ran, the database budget, a failed server update.
kindInfo.test: Sent when a channel is added or tested.

part.head: Heading line
part.url: Link to the post or page

alertStyle.wordingInfo: In your message language. Words in braces, like <c>'{'store'}'</c>, are filled in: leave them as they are.
alertStyle.saved: Saved: your next messages of this kind look like this.
alertStyle.resetHint: Defaults shown: Save to keep them.
alertStyle.sendExample: Send this example to my channels
alertStyle.sent: Sent to {count, plural, one {# channel} other {# channels}} (as saved).

alertHistory.title: Alert history
alertHistory.info: Every message Tora sent you on Telegram or Discord, newest first, as plain text. Kept {days} days.

schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.info: When things run on the server. Its hourly check is heard from here; each collector's time is last night's, moved to the next collect.
schedule.noChecks: No check heard from the server yet (each run of `pnpm collect:request` is one).
schedule.stale: No check heard from the server since {last}: is it on, and is its hourly collect timer running?
schedule.checks: The server checks every {every} min: last {last}, next {next}.
schedule.nextCollectUnknown: Next daily collect: at the first check after midnight.
schedule.notToday: Today's collect has not run yet (last: {at}, {level}): it runs at the next check.
schedule.requested: A "collect now" waits for the next check ({at}).

stepInfo.rankings: (the sites' popularity lists; new candidates collected the same night)
stepInfo.collectors: (one after another; each needs the site to answer)
stepInfo.closing: (pictures, lot sizes: the last 14 days nightly and all of them weekly, value history, buy timing, rule tests, opportunities)

schedule.estimate: Times are estimates: the collect waits up to 5 minutes at random before it starts, and a site may answer slower or faster than last night.

other.morning: The morning check: every day from {hour} (app time), "nothing ran" alerts and the daily summaries.
other.feed: The store feed check: every 2 minutes (a silent feed or board is told).

activity.title: Activity
activity.info: What happened, newest first. Admins see the whole app; everyone sees their own imports.
activity.import: {imported} added, {existing} already in Tora, {skipped} left out, {problem} with a problem
activity.dbBudget: Database: {read} million rows read this month, {projected} million at this pace (budget {budget} million)
activity.sourceQuiet: {sources}: no new sales on the last 3 days of runs (usually some)
activity.selfCheck: Self-check: saved prices differed from the sales and were rebuilt ({items})

admin.trackHour: Board tracker: an hour outside the hours
admin.trackUntilStart: Board tracker: until the start of the hours

activity.listingsGone: {count, plural, one {# listing set aside} other {# listings set aside}}: page gone 3 nights in a row

watchlist.intro: Items you want to buy, in the condition you want, with today's market price. Items at or under your target come first.
watchlist.addIntro: Pick an item already in Tora or add a new one, then the condition you want and, if you like, a target price. It is collected like the items you own.
watchlist.empty: Nothing watched yet. Watch an item to follow its price before buying.
watchlist.conditionHint: The condition you want to buy it in: prices are followed in this condition.
watchlist.targetHint: Optional. You get an alert when the price reaches it.
watchlist.targetHintRetail: Optional. You get an alert when the price reaches it. Retail price: {amount}.
watchlist.cardInfo: Watch this item to follow its price in a condition and set a target price.
watchlist.cardWatched: You watch this item in these conditions.
watchlist.removeConfirm: Stop watching this item in this condition?
watchlist.setupText: Before Tora tells you when to buy, pick a buy strategy for each kind of item you watch. Try each on an example first; Tora suggests one.
watchlist.alertLimited: Alert on Good price even with limited data

opportunities.title: Opportunities
opportunities.intro: Items worth a look within their group of similar items, from the prices Tora collects. Only signals that worked on past prices rank items: each shows how often the price was higher 90 days later. Never a sure thing.
opportunities.updated: Worked out after the collect of {day}.
opportunities.none: Nothing yet: the opportunities are worked out after the next collect.
opportunities.noneProven: No item of this type has a proven signal today.
opportunities.alsoOn: {count, plural, one {# more item has} other {# more items have}} signals on today that are not proven.
opportunities.record: Higher 90 days later {higher} of {checked} times ({pct}; any day {any}).
opportunities.recordFew: Too few past signals to judge ({checked}).
opportunities.recordsIntro: Each signal tested on the group's past prices: every week, the first day of each stretch it was on, checked 90 days later. Proven: 10 or more checks and 5 points or more better than buying on any day (a warning: worse). Most of this history is a rising market, which flatters signals that follow a rise; they are tested again after every collect.

why.sales_up: {sales30} sales in 30 days, {before} a month before.
why.sales_down: {sales30} sales in 30 days, {before} a month before.
why.strong_for_age: Its last 90 days: {change}; similar items at day {days}: {typical} ({items} items).
why.weak_for_age: Its last 90 days: {change}; similar items at day {days}: {typical} ({items} items).

opportunities.popularIntro: The site's own ranking, read with the collect of {day}. Items nobody tracked in its top 30 are added as candidates and collected while they stay there; how a rank change does as a signal is tested once enough days are saved.

plan.title: Budget and date
plan.intro: Set a budget and a date, then tick what to buy. Each item says when (now at a good price, from a day for a new release, or once it comes under a price) and what it would cost, from its buy timing and your strategy. Never a sure thing.
plan.empty: Nothing to plan yet: items with a proven signal and your watches show here.
plan.total: {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}: {total}, {left} {over, select, over {over budget} other {left}}.
plan.late: {count, plural, one {# comes} other {# come}} after your date.
plan.undated: {count, plural, one {# waits} other {# wait}} for a price (no day).

forSale.title: For sale now
forSale.info: Lowest asking price per condition, read with the nightly collect ({date}). Asking prices, not sales.
forSale.none: Nothing reported yet. The nightly collect reads what is for sale on the sources that show it.
forSale.lotOnly: looks like a lot, left out

strategy.title: Buy strategy
strategy.intro: How Tora decides that a price is good to buy at. Pick one for each kind of item you watch or own; try each on the three examples first. A target price on a watch always counts too.
strategy.suggestAll: {count, plural, one {One kind of item uses} other {# kinds of item use}} Tora's suggestion until you choose.
strategy.noTypes: Watch an item first: the strategies are chosen per kind of item.
strategy.notAdvice: Worked out from past prices only: no strategy is a sure thing.
strategy.chartLegend: Daily prices over the example, against its average. Dots: the days this strategy would have said good price.
strategy.calls: {count, plural, =0 {No buy days} one {# buy day} other {# buy days}}

about.steady: Good price in the cheapest quarter of the last 180 days. With little history, 10% under the usual price. Waits while the price or its market falls fast, and while a new release is younger than the age similar items usually hit their low at.
about.bargain: Only the cheapest tenth of the last year. Rare calls, deeper discounts. Waits while the price or its market falls fast, and on new releases.
about.margin: {margin}% under the usual price (the median of the last 180 days). Waits while the price or its market falls fast, and on new releases.
about.dip: Like Steady, but still says good price while the price or its market falls fast, or on a new release, with a warning. Buys earlier; may buy before the bottom.
about.target: No zone: only the target prices you set on your watches.

strategy.exampleIntro: Three fixed examples, the same for everyone: real price histories with the item hidden and the prices rescaled.

exampleAbout.steady: A card over a year: no trend, with dips along the way.
exampleAbout.fall: A box falling for months, then flat, then starting to recover.
exampleAbout.new_set: A box from its release: hype, a dip over the first months, then a recovery. Strategies other than Catch the dip wait 90 days after release.

buy.title: Buy timing
buy.notYet: Worked out after the next collect.

basis.quarter180: the cheapest quarter of the last 180 days
basis.tenth365: the cheapest tenth of the last year
basis.thin_margin: 10% under the usual price: not enough history for a range

buy.falling: Falling fast ({pct} in 2 weeks): wait until it flattens.
buy.fallingDip: Still falling fast ({pct} in 2 weeks): it may go lower.
buy.askInZone: A listing is in the zone now.

limitedWhy.short_range: under 10 days with sales in 180 days

reason.fair: Market value <n>{amount}</n> ({count, plural, one {# sale} other {# sales}} in 30 days)
reason.position: At or below the price on {pct}% of the last 180 days
reason.pattern: Similar items ({items}{group}) moved {pct} in the 90 days after day {days} from release
reason.noPattern: New-set pattern: not enough similar items with prices at this age yet
reason.noRelease: New-set pattern: no release date (only the first collected sale)
reason.noMarket: Similar items: too few to judge the market (5 needed)
reason.ageFirstSale: First collected sale {days} days ago (no release date, so no new-release wait)
reason.lowAge: Similar items ({items}{group}) usually hit their first-year low around day {age}
reason.noLowAge: Too few similar items with a full first year to learn when prices bottom out: day {wait} is used
reason.pastFirstYear: Past its first year: no new-release wait or pattern

buy.marketFalling: The market is falling: similar items ({items}{group}) are {pct} over 12 weeks. Wait until it flattens.
buy.marketFallingDip: The market is still falling: similar items ({items}{group}) are {pct} over 12 weeks. It may go lower.
buy.newRelease: New release ({days} days): similar items ({items}{group}) usually hit their first-year low around day {wait}. Wait until then.
buy.newReleaseDefault: New release ({days} days): new releases often drop in their first months. Wait until day {wait} (too few similar items with a full first year to learn when).
buy.newReleaseDip: New release ({days} days): prices often drop until about day {wait}. It may go lower.

ruleTest.title: Rule test
ruleTest.about: {name} on the whole price history of similar items ({items}{group}).
ruleTest.notYet: Worked out after the next collect.
ruleTest.few: Not enough past signals to test yet: {count} with a price 90 days later ({min} needed).
ruleTest.result: higher 90 days later {higher} of {checked} times ({pct}%), typical change {change}
ruleTest.anyResult: higher 90 days later {pct}% of the time, typical change {change}
ruleTest.better: Better than buying on any day, in the past.
ruleTest.worse: Worse than buying on any day, in the past: the zone paid less, but prices often kept falling for a while.
ruleTest.same: About the same as buying on any day, in the past.
ruleTest.how: Past prices only: a test, not a promise. A signal is the first day of each stretch at Good price, each day judged on the prices before it (without the market check and the new-set pattern). Worked out {date}.

setLines.title: Set lines
setLines.info: A set's place in its franchise's releases. Group studies (the new-set pattern, the new-release wait, the market) compare an item with items of its own line when there are enough (3 or more), else with the whole group. Japanese Pokemon sets get their line from the official set title (拡張パック, 強化拡張パック, ハイクラスパック, anniversary); other items are marked by hand on their edit page.

lineField.label: Set line
lineField.hint: Group studies compare it with items of the same line when there are enough (Settings > Admin preferences > Categories has the list).

opening.title: Opening value
opening.listIntro: Your booster boxes side by side: today's box price against what opening one returns on average from its hit cards (after the selling fee). Best return first.
opening.listEmpty: None of your booster boxes has pull rates yet.
opening.verdictPays: Opening pays at today's price: a box's hit cards bring {breakEven} on average.
opening.verdictLoses: Opening loses at today's price: it pays only below {breakEven}, what a box's hit cards bring on average.
opening.verdictNoPrice: A box's hit cards bring {breakEven} on average: opening pays below that box price.
opening.spread: One box in ten brings less than {low}, one in ten more than {high}.
opening.atRetail: At retail ({retail}) a box returns {back} on average.
opening.notAdvice: Pull rates are community estimates, not official; cards below the hit rarities count as nothing. Not advice.
opening.carryInfo: Each card's price after the fee, how often a box holds it, and its part of a box's average value.
opening.noCards: No cards found for these rarities: check the set code and rarities in Settings > Admin > Box opening.
opening.notRead: Cards not read yet: the next nightly collect reads them.
opening.noRates: No pull rates for this set yet.
opening.noSet: This box is not linked to a catalog set, so its pull rates are unknown.
opening.footer: {packs} packs a box; {fee}% selling fee taken off; cards read {read}.
opening.settingsInfo: Pull rates per set for the box opening value, the sets of the booster boxes anyone tracks. Rates are not official: Tora suggests community numbers, correct them here. Cards are read again once a week, and at the next collect after a change of code or rarities.
opening.fee: Selling fee taken off every card
opening.noBoxes: No booster box with a catalog set is tracked yet.
opening.cardsRead: {count, plural, one {# card} other {# cards}} read {date}

error.code: Type the set code as card titles show it, e.g. SV2a.
error.packs: Packs a box: a whole number from 1 to 100.
error.tiers: Each rarity needs letters (SAR, AR...) and how many a box holds: 3, 0.2 or 1/6.

stores.title: Stores
stores.intro: Notices when people post that cards are on sale in a store near you. Choose your area (stores you pick, or a distance from where you are), switch stores on or off, and go to travel mode when you are away.
stores.pointInfo: Only a rough point is kept (about 100 m), never an address. Press the button again after moving.
stores.filter: Find a store, chain, area or code
stores.noStores: No stores yet: a store list plug-in fills them at the next collect.
stores.extraCodes: Codes posters use, separated by commas
stores.codesEdit: Codes posters use for this store, the store list's too: remove a wrong one or move it to another store. Past posts are matched again.
stores.feedNever: No feed has sent anything yet.
stores.feedStopped: Silent for {minutes} min ({source}): notices stop while the feed is off.
stores.tokenOnce: Copy it now: it is shown only once. The old token stops working.
stores.feedHelp: A feed (for example a userscript in your own browser on the board page) sends new posts with this token. See docs/store-feeds.md.
stores.postsInfo: Posts about your area's stores first.

error.area: That area could not be saved.
error.travel: Travel mode needs an area and an end date.
error.noLocation: The browser did not give a location (allow it in the browser's settings).

stores.noticesTo: Notices for {stores, plural, one {# store} other {# stores}} go to {channels}, as soon as a feed brings a new post about one.
stores.noChannel: No Discord or Telegram connected yet: notices have nowhere to go.
stores.silentAfter: Tell me when the feed is silent for
stores.unknownAlerts: Tell me about posts naming no store or place Tora knows (questions and chat too)
stores.feedAlertsInfo: No silent failures: the app checks every 2 minutes while it runs on this PC. A whole page of new posts at once (posts maybe missed) is always told.
stores.addInfo: For a chain or an area Tora has no list for. A place (an area's name or emoji, with its location) is matched on every board; a store only on its chain's board.
stores.name: Name
stores.locationHelp: Right-click the spot in Google Maps and click the numbers to copy them, then paste here; or use where you are.
stores.codesHelp: what posters write, separated by commas

addError.chain: Chain key: lower-case letters, digits, - or _.
addError.name: Give it a name.
addError.location: Location: two numbers, latitude and longitude.
addError.glossary: A code and its meaning (code up to 20 characters).

stores.codesInfo: What the codes posters use stand for, from the store lists (codes that are just the name left out).
stores.productCodesInfo: Named in notices next to the store ("Megastore Minato · Snow set"). From the board's own list, and the ones admins add (these count anywhere in a post; the board's one-letter codes only among other codes).
stores.noProductCodes: None yet: the board's list comes with the feed's next push.
stores.boardsChosen: Chosen here: the feed follows at its next visit and says which boards it tracks.
stores.boardsByFeed: Ticked: what the feed watches now (set in its menu). Changing it here makes Tora's choice win.
stores.postsInfoPaged: Newest first; more load as you scroll.
stores.byStoreInfo: A chain's board as posted, codes spelled out under each post; pick one of its stores to see only that store.
stores.noRecent: No posts about these stores in the last {hours} hours.
stores.nowInfo: Today's posts by location, the newest first; open one to see each store's posts.
stores.noToday: No posts about these stores today yet.
stores.byLocationInfo: Locations of your area with posts since yesterday (5:00), nearest first, with how many; open one to see its posts, newest first.
stores.quietLocations: {n, plural, one {# location without posts since yesterday} other {# locations without posts since yesterday}}
stores.unread: {n, plural, one {# new message} other {# new messages}}
stores.waiting: {n, plural, one {# new message: show} other {# new messages: show}}

pill.none: Feed not connected: set it up
pill.stoppedTitle: Board tracker is stopped: out of tracking hours ({hours})
pill.resumes: It starts again at about {time}. No posts, replies or pictures are read until then.
pill.silentTitle: Board tracker is not running: nothing received since {time}
pill.silentInfo: No store notices until it sends again. Check the browser tab with the board open (the userscript).
pill.extra: Tracking outside regular hours until {time}, as an admin asked.

accounts.newInfo: Makes the account and a one-time setup link (24 hours). Send the link to the person: they choose their own password and add Tora to their authenticator app on their own device. You never see their password.
accounts.linkReady: Setup link (shown once, send it to the person):
accounts.linkInfo: Works once, until {until}. A new link stops this one.

error.invalid: That code did not match (each code works once: wait for the next one).
error.locked: Too many attempts. Try again later.

accounts.collectInfo: The home PC collects once a night; it checks for a request every hour.
accounts.collectConfirm: Ask the home PC to collect now? It starts within the hour, if it is on.
accounts.collectWaiting: Collect requested at {at}: waiting for the home PC (it checks every hour).
accounts.collectTaken: Collect requested: the home PC started it at {at}.

setup.title: Set up your account

info.both: Choose a password for {username} and add Tora to your authenticator app.
info.2fa: Add Tora to your new authenticator app ({username}).

setup.currentCodeHint: Lost it? One of your backup codes works too.
setup.scanInfo: Scan with your authenticator app (Google Authenticator, 1Password...), or type the key below, then enter the code it shows.
setup.done: Done. Every device was signed out: sign in again.
setup.backupInfo: Each works once if you lose the authenticator. Keep them offline: they are shown only now.

error.expired: This link no longer works (used, expired or replaced). Ask the admin for a new one.
error.locked: Too many attempts. Try again later.
error.short: The password needs at least 12 characters.
error.invalid: That did not match. Try again.
error.newCode: The authenticator's code did not match (check the phone's clock is automatic).
